en: Most monolingual speakers think that other languages are basically just their language
zh: 多數只會說一種語言的人，認為其他語言基本上就是其母語

en: with different words in a slightly different order and maybe a different way of writing.
zh: 換成不同字詞、變換一下排列順序或寫法不同而已。

en: Turns out, though, that there are lots of interesting features in other languages, some
zh: 然而，其他語言有很多有趣的特色，其中一些

en: of which English would really benefit from having. I'm going to talk about four of them.
zh: 要是為英文所有將大有益處。我現在來講其中四種。

en: Number one: Time independence.
zh: 第一：時間獨立性。

en: If you want to describe an activity in English you have to say when it happened, or when
zh: 如果你要用英文表達一個動作，你得說出其發生時間，

en: it will happen. You have to. That's how verbs conjugate. I danced -- past. I am dancing,
zh: 或將發生的時間。你非得這樣，這就是動詞語尾變化。

en: I dance -- present. I will dance -- future. There is no way in English to describe the
zh: 在英文裡沒辦法

en: concept of a person and dancing, but not to mention anything about time. Chinese, on the other hand? Verbs do not conjugate.
zh: 描述關於「人在跳舞」的概念而不提到時間。另一方面，中文沒有語尾變化，

en: In most cases, the meaning is obvious from context. I don't mean to imply that Chinese
zh: 通常前後文的意思已經很清楚了。我不是指中文

en: doesn't have a tense system, just that it's not a requirement. It's not baked into every single sentence.
zh: 完全沒有時態，但並非絕對必要，它並非烙印在每個句子裡。

en: Side note: tenses aren't as simple as past, present and future, and there's some lovely
zh: 附註：時態並非過去、現在、未來那麼簡單，其他語言

en: subtle tenses in other languages. More on that in a later video.
zh: 有些微妙的時態變化。以後的影片會詳細介紹。

en: Anyway, if you want to write poetry with a more vague sense of time: Chinese is one of the languages to choose.
zh: 總之，如果你想用比較模糊的時間觀寫詩，中文是你的選項之一。

en: Number two: Clusivity.
zh: 第二：包含式。

en: The word "we" is confusing. Imagine going up to someone and saying "we've just won the lottery!"
zh: 「我們」一詞容易產生混淆。想像你跟一個人說「我們剛中樂透耶！」 「我們」一詞容易產生混淆。想像你跟一個人說「嘿！我們剛中樂透耶！」

en: There are two possible meanings there. Number 1: "we" refers to the speaker and the listener.
zh: 這邊有兩種可能：1.「我們」包含說者和聽者，

en: We've just won the lottery! Brilliant! Number 2: "we" refers to the speaker and the speaker's
zh: 「我們剛中樂透耶~太爽啦！」 2.「我們」包含說者和說者的朋友......

en: friends... but not the listener. We've just won the lottery! But you haven't.
zh: 但不包含聽者。「我們剛中樂透但你還沒中過，顆顆」

en: In languages with clusivity, there are different words for "we", depending on whether you're
zh: 在擁有包含式的語言，「我們」有不同詞彙，取決於

en: including the listener or not. It shows up in languages in South Asia, Australasia, and
zh: 是否包含聽者。這出現在南亞、澳大拉西亞、

en: all over the world... apart from Europe. And I really wish English had clusivity, because
zh: 世界各地、歐洲除外。我超希望英文有包含式，

en: once you describe it, it's a blindingly obvious missing thing that we -- er, we all -- could really use.
zh: 因為當你描述事情，這顯然是我們─包含聽者─很好用的東西。因為當你描述事情，這顯然是我們─包含聽者─很好用的東西。

en: Number three: Absolute directions.
zh: 第三：絕對方位。

en: This isn't all that useful, but it is cool. In a few languages, notably a couple of Australian
zh: 這不總是實用，但很酷。在少數語言，尤其某些澳洲原住民語言

en: ones like Guugu Yimithirr -- that's the one that's been extensively studied -- there are
zh: 如依密舍語，被廣泛研究的其中一種，裡面沒有所謂

en: no words for left, right, forward or backward. Instead, you always use cardinal directions:
zh: 「左」、「右」、「前」、「後」，你非得使用絕對方位：

notes.zh: 向前（move forward：走出低谷繼續前進）
notes.example: Mistakes are just feedback to help us move forward.

en: the equivalent words for north, south, east and west. In this studio, north is that way,
zh: 「東」、「西」、「南」、「北」。在本間工作室，北邊往那個方向，

en: so right now, I have a north foot and a south foot. If I turn, I now have a west foot and
zh: 所以此刻我有「北腳」和「南腳」。如果轉身，我就有「西腳」和「東腳」。

en: an east foot. I think. I'm having trouble tracking something simple like that: but if
zh: 應該啦。我連這麼簡單的東西都很難定位，但若你

en: you're a native speaker of a language with absolute direction, your brain just handles
zh: 是個母語只有絕對方位的人，你的大腦完全應付得來。

en: it. You always know which way you're pointing -- and if you don't, you have trouble speaking.
zh: 你永遠知道你指的是哪方位，否則就講不出話了。

en: As a language feature, I'd say relative directions are a lot more useful, particularly
zh: 作為語言特性，我得說相對方位更實用些，特別是

en: for those of us that go on the London Underground often -- but it'd be great to always know which way was north.
zh: 那些常搭倫敦地鐵的人，但若你想知道哪條路往北絕對方位就很有用了。

en: Number four: evidentiality.
zh: 最後第四：示證式。

en: In the same way that time is baked into English sentences, there are languages all over the
zh: 如同時態被烙印在英文語句，世上有些語言

en: world where evidence is baked in. If you're reporting something that happened, you have
zh: 烙印著其資訊來源。如果你在報導發生了某事，你得

en: to include whether you personally witnessed it or not. You can do this in English, of
zh: 表明你是否目擊此事。當然你能用英文表達這些：

en: course: "I saw that", "I heard that", but it's not required. Some have five or more
zh: 「I saw that」、「I heard that」，但這非必要。有些語言包含五種或更多種類的

en: different categories of evidence, based on whether you saw it with your own eyes, experienced
zh: 消息來源表示法，基於你是否親眼目睹、

en: it firsthand but it didn't involve seeing anything, whether you've inferred it from
zh: 並未看見卻親身經歷、是否從其他資訊推斷、

en: something else, whether you're reporting what someone else said... all these concepts, which
zh: 是否引用他人說法......這些在英文裡

notes.zh: Can I get you anything else?：餐廳服務生標準詢問句
notes.example: Can I get you anything else, like water?

en: are complicated to explain in English, are expressed just by how you change the ending of a word.
zh: 極其複雜難以表達的概念，你只需要動動字尾即可。極其複雜難以表達的概念，你只需要動動字尾即可。

en: These fantastic features are one of the reasons why keeping minor languages alive is important.
zh: 這些美妙特性就是為何保留弱勢語言非常重要的原因。

en: If English had dominated the world and stamped out every other tongue, then we'd lose not
zh: 要是英文徹底征服世界並消滅所有語言，我們不只失去

en: only these rich languages, but we'd lose the insights that we gain of what the human mind's capable of.
zh: 這些豐富的語言，也失去其能幫助了解人類心智可能性的內涵。這些豐富的語言，也失去其能幫助了解人類心智可能性的內涵。

en: So here's my question to you: can you think of a brand new language feature. Something
zh: 這是今天問題：你能想出一種新語言特性，

en: that every language should have, but doesn't.
zh: 各種語言都應該有卻沒有嗎？

en: Next time: why things aren't always black and white. Or blue and green.
zh: 下集預告：為何事物不是非黑即白，或非藍即綠。

notes.zh: give the green light：開綠燈、准許行動
notes.example: Management finally gave our proposal the green light.
